lead.headline: Bears Win Five Straight, Move to 8-2
lead.subhead: Chicago beat New Orleans 21-13 at Soldier Field. Caleb Williams threw two touchdowns, Jeffery Simmons had three of six sacks, and Montez Sweat forced a safety. Not pretty. Still a win. Stack them.

articles.hed: Murray 45, Jokic Triple-Double Sink the Bulls in OT
articles.body: Denver won 151-145 in overtime. Jamal Murray scored a season-high 45 with eight in OT; Nikola Jokic had 37, 18 and 11. Josh Giddey answered with 23 points, 14 boards and a career-high 22 assists for Chicago. Great nights lose to greater finishes.

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds squares the mind. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then go build.

mindset.body: The Bears didn't play clean yesterday. They won anyway, five in a row, 8-2. Murray put up 45 and needed every one of the eight he scored in overtime. Nobody remembers how pretty it was. They remember who finished. Three work days this week: ship one real 7EightMade piece before Wednesday ends. Competitive. Unbeatable. Always rising. fall down 7 stand up 8.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Monday, the Moon's day: run this right after Morning Charge. It's clear and about 31 out, so do the RipStick finisher in the garage or swap in 60 seconds of fast feet. Smooth, controlled reps.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom's RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time.

Monday belongs to the Moon, which the old magicians tied to cycles, tides and the hidden life of habit. Lunar work was about rhythm: what you repeat, you become.
The German mystic (c. 1260-1328) taught 'letting go' (Gelassenheit): drop the clutter and the essential shows up. Subtraction as a spiritual practice.
Gnostic texts describe a divine spark asleep inside each person, waiting to be woken by knowledge (gnosis), not belief. The work is waking up.
